requirements.text: Register a high priority case for this issue through phone channel (their SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 Variant 5 with serial prefix P25 at the datacenter)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND account_id = 8 AND contact_id = 10 AND product_id = 25 AND installed_product_id = 40 AND channel = 'phone' AND priority = 'high' AND state = 'new' AND assignment_group_id = 28 AND assigned_to IS NULL AND escalation = 0 AND escalation_reason IS NULL AND reopen_count = 0
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (1233 after 1232); the only case the task creates; number is server-kept and dropped from the benchmark's cells
account 8 is Stark Industries (account 38 'Stark, Petersen and Palmer' is the near-name)

no contact named; contact 10 (Marc Henry, the account's primary contact, is_primary = 1) kept from the benchmark check; contact 11 is on the unit's two existing cases but nothing in the request or policy picks her

installed product 40 is the account's only unit with serial prefix P25 (P25-458046-6504, product 25, in_use); unit 15 with a P25 serial is on account 3; 'at the datacenter' matches no location name (40 sits at 817 'Stark Industries Hq - London'), so account, product and serial decide
state = new from the policy default; assigned_to, escalation, escalation_reason, reopen_count kept from the benchmark check as the untouched registration defaults
short_description not tested: the policy only suggests a template ('can be something like') and the benchmark does not test it

'confirm they have active premium support coverage' is a read: entitlement 74 (account 8, product 25, premium, active, contract 22 active to 2028-07-14) exists on the seed, so nothing in the database changes
disagreement: cells: A includes assignment_group_id = 28, B leaves it to the assignment requirement; chose A's because the benchmark's 'customer_case' check tests it and the fuller set is tighter

requirements.text: assign the case to our Contact Center L1_2 Support Team
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND assignment_group_id = 28
assumptions: group 28 is 'Contact Center L1_2' (type support, active); groups 8 'Contact Center L1', 48 'L1_3' and 68 'L1_4' are the near-names
a cell set on the row the task creates (set_case_assignment_group after create_new_case), so kind is change although the row is new
assignment to the group only; the request names no user, so assigned_to stays null (tested in the create requirement)

requirements.text: Register a high priority case for this issue (policy: knowledge base search on registration, the found article linked as suggested)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_knowledge WHERE case_kb_id = 528 AND case_id = 1233 AND knowledge_id = 38 AND used_as = 'suggested'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (528 after 527); the only link the task creates

implied by the request, not stated: it never asks for knowledge, but the policy makes a knowledge search part of registering a case and links what it finds as suggested, and the tools include retrieve_knowledge and link_case_knowledge; kept from the benchmark check
knowledge 38 is the only article for product 25 on the seed (KB-0000038, published, internal), so the choice is fixed

requirements.text: assign the case (boundary: the existing open cases on the same installed product)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id IN (182, 198) AND assignment_group_id = 28
assumptions: cases 182 (in_progress, no group) and 198 (new, group 19) are the open cases on account 8 for product 25 and unit 40; a reading of 'the case' that picks an existing case for this issue instead of the registered one would assign one of them

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on the case (1233), its assignment (group 28), the knowledge link (528, article 38, suggested) and all three dispositions (kept). disagreement: create cells: A includes assignment_group_id = 28, B leaves it to the assignment requirement; kept A's as the benchmark check's fuller set (logged in the requirement). disagreement: stay on cases 182 and 198 not taking group 28 (B only); kept because it is the boundary of 'the case': the open cases on the same unit are what a reading that reuses an existing case would assign. The benchmark's two customer_case checks overlap (the first already tests assignment_group_id = 28); both are kept, one per thing asked. No location is named 'datacenter'; the unit is fixed by account, product and serial prefix. The entitlement confirmation (entitlement 74) is read-only and leaves no database trace, so it has no requirement; entitlement 77 is the premium one for product 25 that is inactive on an expired contract. The knowledge link is the judgement call: the request never says 'investigate', so the policy's search-and-link rule applies on a broad reading of registering a case for a live issue; the benchmark's check is the prior. Case 182 already links article 38 (row 76), so a stay on links to the existing cases would not discriminate and is left out.
